## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ekādhippāyakathā* (Kv 23.1) is a doctrinal controversy located in the twenty-third chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, a treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The controversy addresses the heterodox proposition that sexual intercourse (*methuno dhammo*) may be engaged in when motivated by a single, united intention or common purpose (*ekādhippāya*) [Rahula 1956; Bareau 1955]. As noted in the commentary, such a shared purpose was framed by its proponents either as an act of compassion and sympathy or as a joint resolution made at a shrine to be reborn together in a future existence [Rahula 1956]. Against this view, the Theravādin position maintains that sexual intercourse is categorically forbidden to a monastic regardless of intention, constituting an offense of defeat (*pārājika*) that entails immediate expulsion from the community, thereby safeguarding against monastic laxity [Bareau 1955].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any cross-language parallels for this discourse in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan traditions [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus likewise finds no significant Pali-internal text reuse for this section, and SuttaCentral registers one modern translation [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
